# Instructor guide · Topic 9: Linked Lists

<!-- generated by tools/export-docs.mjs from topics/ and questions/: do not edit by hand -->

## Learning objectives

Think in nodes and pointers: traverse, insert, delete and reverse safely, and use dummy nodes and fast/slow pointers.

By the end of the topic, students can:

- **Nodes and pointers:** A linked list is a chain of nodes.
- **Insert, delete, search:** Changing a linked list means changing pointers, in the right order.
- **The dummy node:** Deleting or inserting at the head is a special case… unless you put a fake node before it.
- **Reversing a linked list:** The most important linked-list skill: three pointers (prev, cur, nxt) and four lines, in exactly the right order.
- **Fast and slow pointers:** Two pointers moving at different speeds find the middle in one pass, detect cycles in O(1) space, and locate positions from the end.
- **Doubly linked lists:** Add a prev pointer and you can walk backwards and remove any node in O(1) once you hold it.

## Duration and prerequisites

- Lessons: about **54 minutes** of guided material (6 lessons)
- Practice: 21 coding problems and 37 quick questions in the bank; plan at least as much practice time as lesson time
- Suggested format: one 90-minute session
- Prerequisites: Topic 1 (Python for DSA)

## Live coding demonstrations

- The node class (lesson “Nodes and pointers”)
- Brute force → optimal walkthrough: **Palindrome List: copy to an array → reverse half in place** (Challenge tab). Code the brute force, ask students to find the repeated work, then refactor.
- Visualizers to drive while students predict the next step: Linked list: insert, delete, search, reverse · Fast and slow pointers

## Questions to ask the class

Ask, wait for several answers, then reveal (the answers are on the topic's Review flashcards).

- Access the i-th node?
- Insert at head?
- Why a dummy node?
- Reverse in 4 lines?
- Middle in one pass?
- Cycle in O(1) space?
- Nth from end?
- Doubly linked bonus?

## Classroom exercises (individual, 10–15 minutes each)

- Length of a Linked List (`ll-length`)
- Value at Index k (`ll-kth`)
- Reverse Linked List (`ll-reverse`)

Code tracing on the board: Following pointers (`ll-p1`), Move the head (`ll-p2`), Skip a node (`ll-p3`), Insert at the head (`ll-p4`)

Find-the-bug warm-ups: Reversal loses the rest (`ll-d1`), The last node is ignored (`ll-d2`)

## Pair programming (25–30 minutes)

One driver types, one navigator thinks ahead and checks edge cases; swap every 10 minutes.

- Remove Nth Node From End (`ll-remove-nth`)
- Reverse Between Positions (`ll-reverse-between`)
- Build from scratch: Build a Singly Linked List (`build-linked-list`), Build a Doubly Linked List (`build-dll`), Build an LRU Cache (`build-lru`)

## Homework

- Palindrome Linked List (`ll-palindrome`)
- Linked List Cycle II (start of the cycle) (`ll-cycle-start`)
- Sort a Linked List (`ll-sort`)
- Finish the topic's Review quiz in the browser and clear the revision queue.

## Solutions and grading

- Reference solutions: `solutions/09_linkedlist/` (also behind “Show solution” in the browser).
- Students check their own work with `python dsa.py test <id>`; collect `pytest tests/test_my_solutions.py -k linkedlist` output as evidence.
- Grade with the coding rubric in [README.md](README.md#grading-rubrics).
